title: Lists as Arrays in hazel-jit
blurb: Compiled Hazel keeps a list as cells, so every call converts a page's arrays to cells and back: in Gnome world that is 5% to 70% of a Hazel call's time. A hybrid from 11-23 (cells for ::, array segments for a page's arrays) was not merged; since then crossing goes by declared type, and the lists are what is left. Since: Gnome world's creatures in Floats, an insect 4.7 µs to 0.37; lists as segments built on a trial, a water step 2.38 ms to 1.60, every answer the same.

builds.hazel-jit: hazeljs branch 0f24cea171 (the page); trial/1126-night abf653a21d (the AOT file)

runs.pane: the Claude app's browser pane on the laptop (hidden), Gnome world 0.0.156 at http://localhost:8141/world/?test=1, 2026-11-28 10:20-10:40 MST; compiled code from world/rules-aot.json (hazel-jit, trial/1126-night abf653a21d, the same compiler as the hazeljs branch's 0f24cea171)
runs.recorded: 400 steps of the speed run with every Hazel option on (water, way, plan, rivers, folk) and rain started, each Hazel call's arguments recorded (up to 400 a function); replayed 100 of each: the converters (the AOT file's own wrap) around a stub that returns the compiled answer (the crossing alone), and the compiled code alone given the very arguments the converters made; fresh copies of the page's arguments each call (structuredClone), but a squirrel's tree graph and the hawks' great trees handed over as the same objects each call, as the game does

measures.crossing: the converters in and out around a stub that returns the compiled answer, a mean a call
